changes.before: Convert to character before numeric: as.numeric(as.character(value)). What prints for these labels?
changes.after: A factor stores categories using integer codes and a list of labels called levels.

before: factor(c("20","10"), levels=c("10","20")) stores category labels with integer codes determined by the level order.
as.numeric(factor_value) exposes the underlying category codes. It does not parse the printed category labels as numbers.

as.character first obtains the labels. as.numeric can then parse valid numeric text; unsuitable text can produce NA with a warning, so real input still needs validation.

as.character receives the factor and returns its labels as character text, in observation order. Passing those labels to as.numeric parses the shown valid numeric labels instead of exposing factor codes.
```r
value <- factor(c("20", "10"), levels = c("10", "20"))
labels <- as.character(value)
cat(labels, sep = ",")
cat("\n")
cat(as.numeric(labels), sep = ",")
```
It prints:
```text
20,10
20,10
```

Complete local R example; the app itself does not execute it:
```r
value <- factor(c("20", "10"), levels=c("10", "20"))
cat(as.numeric(value), sep=",")
```
Expected output or behavior: 2,1. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Compare level order, stored codes and labels before interpreting a factor numerically. You may trace it without a R interpreter; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: A factor stores categories using integer codes and a list of labels called levels.
Here label ten is first and label twenty is second.
Converting this factor directly to numbers returns level positions, not the numbers those labels resemble.

Follow the labeled parts of this example.
```r
value <- factor(c("20", "10"), levels=c("10", "20"))
cat(as.numeric(value), sep=",")
```
The output is `2,1`. The input labels twenty and ten therefore give codes two and one.
First convert the factor to its text labels, then read those labels as numbers.
